evidence: I read CONTEXT.txt whole first, then DRAFT.txt, SOURCE.txt and the_change. The draft, “It’s one person doing three jobs rather than getting three more people to move in with you to help with the rent! Each job keeps the others in balance.”, sits once in the section's second paragraph, between “…your wise Guide.” and his unchanged “It’s you that needs to develop these qualities.” CHANGE CHECK: it is Emulate's two sentences in place of his one three-jobs sentence; the rent joke is kept (“to help with the rent”) and the balance is kept word for word from his source (“each job keeps the others in balance”), so his “keeps” is back where Emulate had “helps to keep”. That is what the_change says. MEANING CHECK against SOURCE.txt (“That’s one grown-up doing three jobs, not three more people moving in to help with the rent, and each job keeps the others in balance.”): one agent, three jobs, not three extra people for the rent, and the jobs balancing each other are all present, and no claim or fact is added. The turns are small. “grown-up” becomes “person”: I weighed this, because “grown-up” carries the adult/child contrast, but the heading says “the inner adult’s three jobs”, the sentence before names the “Adult Protector”, and his published guide itself says “the present-day person reparents the inner child”, so the adult sense survives and the next sentence (“It’s you…”) says who the person is. “not three more people moving in” becomes “rather than getting three more people to move in with you”: same hypothetical, and “with you” matches the paragraph's address. The “!” closes the joke. It is the only exclamation mark in this section, so it is the one louder note in a calm paragraph, but it sits on a joke in a casual first-person guide, and the writer says it is Emulate's own turn; I count it as voice and not a seam. SEAM CHECK: the sentence before sets up the three named jobs, the joke answers the obvious misreading that three jobs means three beings, “Each job keeps the others in balance.” adds a new point (the balance) instead of explaining the joke, and his closing sentence still follows. I did not hear a different writer, a hedge or a tidy summary. The two “It’s” sentences (“It’s one person…”, “It’s you…”) echo one person / you more than they repeat idly. TELL ROWS: I went through T01 to T29 and C01 to C04 against the literal draft in its context and found none actually happening. Closest calls: T12, T16 and T18 (the one-versus-three contrast is his own rent joke from the source and answers a real misreading, it is not a reflex “not X, it's Y” and not A/B packaging); T17, T20 and T29 (“Each job keeps the others in balance.” is a short plain sentence, but it is mid-paragraph, it states a claim he made and the change must keep, and it is not an aphorism or a closing summary); T08 (nothing explains the image); T21 (the source's single packed sentence is split, so the draft is the less condensed one); T26 (“job/jobs” and “three” recur because the joke needs exactly that); T15 (no rare-word swaps, “person” is the commoner word). C01 to C04: no naming problem, the referents are clear, no invented first-person fact, no outside claim. LINTER FINDINGS: “B2 contrast” is accepted, because the contrast is the joke and is his own (source: “not three more people moving in”), not a framing device. “B7 short landing at paragraph end” is accepted, because the linter saw the draft alone; in the article this sentence is not the paragraph's end, his “It’s you that needs to develop these qualities.” follows, and neither is a clever closer. “D9 follows the source order” is accepted: a two-point sentence rewritten in its only natural order (one person doing three jobs, then the balance), the joke is an aside that takes the most words, so T13 and T09 are absent. Verdict PASS: it does what the_change says, keeps the source meaning, adds nothing, and reads right in its context.
